newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: FORECAST-DBS Land profit seen healthy.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-DBS Land profit seen healthy.

text.p: DBS Land Ltd is expected to post robust growth of more than 20 percent in net profit for the first half of 1997, investment analysts said over the weekend.
The property arm of the DBS Bank group is expected to release its interim results in the middle of August.

Singapore analysts usually do not give half year forecasts and those polled in The Edinburgh Financial Publishing Estimate Directory have a full year 1997 consensus of Singapore $254.2 million for DBS Land, up 23 percent against the previous year.
A total of 32 analysts gave forecasts ranging from a low of S$239.3 to a high of S$322.1 million.
Analysts said DBS Land's strong 1997 growth, although down from the prior year's 30 percent rise, was due mainly to higher earnings from its overseas projects.
"DBS results should be quite healthy this year with overseas contributions making a significant impact," ING Baring Securities analyst Lim Chung Chun said.
He expected earnings from overseas projects to rise to 19 percent, up from 13 percent previously, of total group pre-tax profit.
The bulk would be from the group's residential projects in Hong Kong and in Australia, through Australand, and also Indonesia.
"Some of the Hong Kong projects will only be launched in the second half so I expect stronger growth in the second half," Vicent Yek, investment analyst with HSBC James Capel said.
Analysts said overseas earnings would become increasingly important against the backdrop of a sluggish Singapore market.
"This will be the last year where there will be huge trading profits from the boom years of 1994 and 1995," Ng Yaw Tong, investment analyst with GK Goh Securities.
Rental income from commercial properties was also expected to dip as one of the group's largest retail malls, Plaza Singapura, has been shut for upgrading.
Analysts appeared divided over how much DBS Land's recent acquisition of a 19.2 percent stake in health-care and property group Parkway Holdings would contribute this year.
The contribution would be more meaningful if DBS Land can equity account Parkway's earnings.
Otherwise, it would only receive dividend income which would not be significant, they said.
Under Singapore law, DBS Land would need to hold at least 20 percent of Parkway or prove it has management control of the company before it can equity account the latter's profits.
Analysts said there was a likelihood that DBS Land would increase its stake in Parkway and probably mount a takeover of the company before the end of the year.
